title: Chiranjeevi and Naga Babu Rush ₹5 Lakh Aid to Gabbar Singh Actor After Brain Stroke
excerpt: The Mega family's latest act of generosity comes as Telugu cinema rallies around character actor Ramesh, who is being treated at Apollo Hospital in Hyderabad.
body:
• Actor Ramesh, known for his role in Pawan Kalyan's blockbuster Gabbar Singh, has suffered a severe brain stroke and is being treated at Apollo Hospital.
  • Megastar Chiranjeevi donated ₹3 lakh and his brother Naga Babu contributed ₹2 lakh, bringing the Mega family's support to ₹5 lakh.
  • Director Harish Shankar, who directed Gabbar Singh, also visited the hospital and provided additional financial assistance.
  • Chiranjeevi has donated over ₹20 lakh for medical emergencies in the Telugu film industry in 2026 alone.

Telugu Cinema Rallies Around One of Its Own

When word spread that character actor Ramesh — a familiar face in Telugu cinema best remembered for his role in Pawan Kalyan's 2012 blockbuster Gabbar Singh — had suffered a severe brain stroke, it took less than a day for the industry's biggest names to respond.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=knyTSTwGBxA

Ramesh is currently undergoing treatment at Apollo Hospital in Hyderabad, where his condition is being closely monitored. Upon learning of the situation, Megastar Chiranjeevi — who has been in regular contact with Dr Subba Reddy at Apollo — personally arranged a ₹3 lakh cheque for the actor's family. His brother, actor-producer Naga Babu, added ₹2 lakh, bringing the Mega family's total contribution to ₹5 lakh.

Chiranjeevi also assured Ramesh's family that he would help them access treatment under the state government's medical health insurance scheme, a gesture that goes beyond the immediate financial aid.

Director Harish Shankar Visits Hospital

Director Harish Shankar, who worked with Ramesh on Gabbar Singh, made a personal visit to Apollo Hospital to check on the actor. During his visit, he offered encouragement to the family and provided further financial assistance. Actor and publicist Vamshi Shekar later shared a photograph of Chiranjeevi and Naga Babu presenting the cheques to Ramesh's family.

https://x.com/CNNnews18/status/2081337864475041803

The solidarity has been swift and public, reflecting the Telugu film industry's tradition of rallying around colleagues in medical distress — a pattern that Chiranjeevi, in particular, has sustained for decades.

Chiranjeevi's Record of Quiet Philanthropy

The Gabbar Singh actor's case is far from the first time Chiranjeevi has stepped in. Through his Chiranjeevi Charitable Trust (CCT), established in 1998, the actor operates one of India's most prominent celebrity-backed blood banks and eye banks.

In early 2026 alone, Chiranjeevi donated over ₹20 lakh toward medical emergencies within the film industry. In April, he contributed ₹10.5 lakh for makeup artist Sivanath's urgent heart surgery at Apollo Hospitals and ₹9.5 lakh for the bypass surgery of KV Narasaiah's wife — Narasaiah being Chiranjeevi's former manager.

In both cases, according to colleagues, Chiranjeevi insisted on paying the full hospital bill himself rather than seeking discounts or free treatment. He recently donated his entire NTR Award prize money of ₹10 lakh to various charitable trusts and an additional ₹5 lakh to the Telugu Film Journalists' Association.

"He does not like to publicize the charity. These news come out only when the beneficiaries tell that to media."

— Industry sources on Chiranjeevi's philanthropic approach

The Broader Safety Net Question

While the generosity of stars like Chiranjeevi is widely celebrated, Ramesh's case also underscores a persistent gap in the Indian film industry: the absence of comprehensive health insurance and retirement benefits for character actors, junior artists and below-the-line crew.

Unlike lead actors who can negotiate seven- and eight-figure per-film fees, character actors and supporting cast members often work without formal contracts or benefits. When a medical emergency strikes, the industry's response depends largely on personal relationships and the willingness of its most successful members to intervene — a system that is generous but not systematic.

What's Next

Ramesh's family has expressed gratitude for the outpouring of support from the Telugu film community. His recovery is being monitored by the medical team at Apollo Hospital, with Chiranjeevi reportedly staying in regular contact. Fans and colleagues continue to pray for his swift recovery.
